sents.t: In early December, I got an email that changed everything.
It was from Harbor Books, a publishing company in Chicago.
Emma had shown them my translations of children’s stories, and they wanted me to join their team as a translator and editor.
The salary was almost twice what I make now.
I read the email five times.
When I was a boy, I used to read books under my blanket with a flashlight.
I used to dream about working with books in two languages.
And now my dream was in my inbox.
But there was a problem.
The job was in Chicago, four hours away from Rosa, from Max, from my team at the bookstore.
And from Lily, whose life is here.
For two days, I couldn’t concentrate at work.
Tina asked me if I was sick.
Finally, I called Emma.
“I knew they would love your work!” she said.
“You’d love Chicago, Sam.”
Then I told Lily.
She was quiet for a long time.
“You should do what makes you happy,” she said at last.
But her eyes looked sad.
That night, I sat with Max on the front steps.
I used to think that following your dream was easy.
Now I know that sometimes you have to choose between two good things.
